messages:
maria_k: Quick summary — ran our replay harness against the optimized kernel set and saw ~18% worse p99 (and occasional OOMs) compared to synthetic. Suspect client-side connection/keepalive + KV cache warming is introducing artefacts. Repro cmd + notes below.

samir: Can you paste the exact harness invocation and the HTTP/gRPC settings you used? Also whether the replay was replaying long sessions (multi-request per conn) or single-request spikes.

maria_k: Sure — using our replay tool that replays recorded user sessions:
```
./replay-driver --trace traces/2025-10-long-sessions.json \n  --concurrency 256 --clients-per-host 64 --grpc=true --tls=true \n  --keepalive-idle=60 --keepalive-interval=10 --pool-size=64
```
Synthetic run used a short synthetic traffic generator: `synthetic-gen --qps 5000 --open-conns 500 --tls=true` (stateless single-request pattern).

olga: Two quick suspects: 1) replay has long-lived sessions with cold KV prefixes so the runtime sees more cache misses; 2) connection reuse. gRPC multiplexes, HTTP client often creates many connections unless keepalive / pool config matches. Did you set TCP_NODELAY?

rahul_g: Also add TLS session resumption and handshake counts — if replay opens connections frequently (or client churns), per-connection TLS + Nagle + congestion interactions can push p99. gRPC (http2) behaves differently because it sends many streams over 1 TCP flow which has different head-of-line and cwnd dynamics.

perf-bot: CI load-run #458 finished. Observed a 20% jump in connection churn and a KV-cache miss-rate increase from 7% -> 31% during replay window 12:34-12:42. Linked metrics: https://internal.metrics/replay-458 (redacted) :chart_with_upwards_trend:

maria_k: I instrumented socket stats: replay shows many short-lived client sockets when the driver batches hosts per thread slightly differently. The synthetic generator keeps connections warm and reuse is high -> higher KV prefix hit-rate and friendly batch sizes for kernels. Pre-warming KV cache before replay reduced p99 by ~12%. Numbers: 
- baseline synthetic p99: 210ms
- replay cold p99: 262ms
- replay + prewarm p99: 231ms
Also saw TLS handshake CPU spikes on worker nodes during replay.

samir: So apples-to-apples needs to match: connection count/concurrency per host, keepalive settings, client-side Nagle/TCP_NODELAY, TLS session reuse, and request inter-arrival patterns. Also ensure the kernel selector isn't picking a different kernel because sequence length distribution changed between synthetic and replay. Did you check selected kernel per request?

maria_k: Good call — kernel selector logs show more fallback to the generic kernel for longer sequences present in replay traces. That combined with cache misses explains regression. When I forced the same kernel (for a quick test) and prewarmed cache, numbers matched synthetic within 4%.

olga: Can we standardize a bench checklist? Minimal items: 
- match client open-conns + pool sizes
- set TCP_NODELAY / document Nagle effects
- match TLS settings including session resumption and SNI behavior
- pre-warm KV cache (or run warmup phase)
- compare kernel selection histograms and sequence-length CDFs
- record socket-level metrics (retransmits, cwnd, RTT)
- run both gRPC and HTTP variants (ALPN differences)

devex-bot: Created PR #213 in infra/benching: add bench-checklist.md with the above items and a warmup harness. Link: https://git.internal/pr/213 :white_check_mark:

maria_k: Thanks — next steps: 1) run replay with explicit keepalive/pool settings to duplicate synthetic config; 2) add a 5 minute prewarm step for KV cache; 3) dump kernel selection histogram and attach; 4) re-run and post p50/p95/p99. I'll kick off a run in ~10m and ping results.

samir: If you want I can help instrument client to force TCP_NODELAY and log connection reuse counts per thread. That would prove/disprove Nagle angle quickly.

maria_k: Appreciate it — will take you up on that. Will post the run link when ready. :thumbsup:
